primary_secondary.note: Own production deployment and before/after measurement.

study_type.claude: Case study (industrial case study / experience report with pre/post observational evaluation)
study_type.nlm: Case study (empirical case study / longitudinal pre-post observational study)
study_type.note: Claude also frames it as an industrial experience report (single author, practitioner blueprint).

research_method.claude: Industrial case study / experience report of a production deployment; observational pre- vs. post-adoption comparison (~12 months) with DORA and quality metrics; qualitative developer survey; two illustrative cases (cross-service rollout, LLM bug triage)
research_method.nlm: Empirical case study with longitudinal pre-post observational comparison over 12 months; DORA-grounded evaluation; telemetry, CI/CD, VCS/PR, issue tracker data; qualitative developer surveys
research_method.value: Single-organization industrial case study of a governance-first AI-augmented SDLC blueprint deployed in production; observational pre- vs. post-adoption comparison over two adjacent periods (~12 months) using DORA, quality and throughput metrics from CI/CD logs, VCS/PR analytics, test infrastructure, issue tracker and observability; two illustrative cases (cross-service attribute rollout, LLM bug triage); qualitative developer survey; no randomization or statistical tests
research_method.note: Number of developers and survey respondents not reported.

context.claude: Industry: global e-commerce platform 'RetailCo' (pseudonym), hundreds of microservices, polyglot codebases, CI/CD; multiple teams; number of developers not reported
context.nlm: Industry: global e-commerce platform 'RetailCo' (eBay Inc.), hundreds of microservices, polyglot codebases; 1 organization
context.value: industry; single global e-commerce company ('RetailCo', anonymized) with hundreds of microservices and polyglot codebases, multiple teams; number of developers not reported
context.note: NotebookLM equates RetailCo with eBay (author's affiliation); the paper only says 'RetailCo, anonymized'.

dora_applied.note: DORA metrics are the basis of the before/after evaluation framework.

space_applied.note: Claude: not mentioned; NotebookLM: referenced only. 'SPACE' does not occur in the full text.

ai_discussed.note: LLM assistants across the SDLC (IDE copilot, PR reviewer, test generation, AIOps, bug triage).

remote_covid.note: NotebookLM's 'distributed multi-team environment' refers to microservice teams, not remote work.

data_window.claude: ~12 months (two adjacent pre/post periods; no dates)
data_window.value: ~12 months across two adjacent pre-/post-adoption periods (calendar dates not stated)

cat_productivity.note: Task execution time (-40%), story points per sprint per developer (+10–15%), manual bug triage hours, capacity uplift.

cat_quality.note: Change failure rate, MTTR, defect density per KLOC, automated test coverage.

cat_collaboration.note: Thin: code-review metric (first-round PR approvals 85% → 92%); Claude labels it Quality/Collaboration, NotebookLM Quality/Process.

cat_satisfaction.note: Both label perceived productivity/focus as DevEx/Satisfaction, but it is perceived productivity (cat_survey); no satisfaction or well-being measure.

cat_activity.note: PRs merged per team per week (+12%); AI suggestion acceptance telemetry.

cat_delivery.note: Deployment frequency (1 → 20/week), lead time for changes, feature delivery cycle, dev-to-merge cycle time.

cat_devex.note: NotebookLM says DevEx referenced; only generic 'developer experience' in the text.

cat_agile.note: Borderline: story points per sprint is counted as a productivity/throughput metric by both; no ceremony or process metric.

cat_survey.note: Developer survey: >80% perceived productivity gains; ~95% affirm need for human code review.

evidence.quote: We compared metrics across two adjacent periods totaling ∼ 12 months (pre-adoption vs. postadoption), covering multiple teams and services.
evidence.loc: PDF p. 6 (D. Measurement Methodology and Validity)

evidence.quote: Data sources included CI/CD logs (deploy frequency, lead time), VCS/PR analytics (cycle time, approvals), test infrastructure (coverage)
evidence.loc: PDF p. 6 (D. Measurement Methodology and Validity)

evidence.quote: We evaluate outcomes using both quantitative productivity and reliability metrics and qualitative developer feedback.
We deployed this blueprint at a global e-commerce company ("RetailCo") and achieved a 20× increase in deployment frequency without any loss of reliability.
We provide a quantitative before/after evaluation framework based on DORA metrics to measure AI's impact on productivity and reliability.

the organization's deployment frequency increased from 1 to 20 per week (≈ 20×), and lead times for changes shrank from multiple weeks to under one week, all while post-release failure rates decreased.
Change Failure Rate (%) MTTR (hours) Defect Density (per KLOC) Automated Test Coverage (%)
Task execution time decreased by ≈ 40% with AI assistance

Completed story points per sprint per developer rose ∼ 10-15% (with guidance to avoid point inflation). PRs merged per team per week increased ∼ 12%. First-round approvals improved (∼ 85% →∼ 92%), as AI pre-flagged minor issues

evidence.loc: PDF p. 6 (C. Developer Experience (Qualitative); two-column extraction splits 'productivity')

evidence.quote: ∼ 95% affirmed the continued necessity of human code review, consistent with human-in-the-loop guardrails.
